wins.label: Strong data center growth
wins.evidence: Data Center segment revenue grew 38% year-over-year and 43% sequentially to a record $2.3 billion.

wins.label: EPYC server CPU demand
wins.evidence: Significant double-digit percentage growth in fourth-gen EPYC processor revenue and demand for our third-gen EPYC processor portfolio.

wins.label: MI300X GPU success
wins.evidence: MI300X GPUs deliver leadership generative AI performance by combining our high-performance CDNA 3 architecture with industry-leading memory bandwidth and capacity.

wins.label: AI software ecosystem expansion
wins.evidence: The ROCm 6 stack significantly increases performance in key generative AI workloads, adds expanded support and optimizations for additional frameworks and libraries.

wins.label: Strong client segment growth
wins.evidence: Client segment revenue was $1.5 billion, an increase of 62% year-over-year.

risks.label: Gaming segment decline
risks.evidence: Gaming segment revenue declined 17% year-over-year and 9% sequentially to $1.4 billion.

risks.label: Embedded segment weakness
risks.evidence: Embedded segment revenue decreased 24% year-over-year and 15% sequentially to $1.1 billion.

risks.label: Supply chain constraints
risks.evidence: First half capacity is tight and more comes on in the second half of the year.

risks.label: Competitive pressures
risks.evidence: Intel is adopting chiplet technology and may be ahead in process technology.

risks.label: Inventory normalization
risks.evidence: Embedded segment demand will remain soft through the first half of the year as customers continue to focus on normalizing their inventory levels.

wins.label: Strong Data Center Sales in 2023
wins.evidence: We finished 2023 strong as data center sales accelerated significantly throughout the year despite the mixed demand environment.

wins.label: Record Data Center Revenue
wins.evidence: We delivered record data center segment annual revenue and strong top line and bottom line growth in the fourth quarter, driven by the ramp of Instinct AI accelerators and robust demand for EPYC server CPUs.

wins.label: MI300X Revenue Exceeded Expectations
wins.evidence: Revenue exceeding our $400 million expectation for MI300X GPUs in the fourth quarter.

wins.label: Significant EPYC CPU Adoption
wins.evidence: North American hyperscalers expanded fourth-gen EPYC processor deployments to power their internal workloads and public instances.

wins.label: Strong Customer Traction for Turin
wins.evidence: Customer excitement for our upcoming Turin family of EPYC processors is very strong. Turin is a drop-in replacement for existing fourth-gen EPYC platforms that extends our performance, efficiency and TCO leadership.

risks.label: Mixed Demand Environment
risks.evidence: Despite strong results, we finished 2023 with mixed demand environment.

risks.label: Server CPU Shipment Decline
risks.evidence: Shipments of AMD’s server CPUs declined north of 20% year-over-year.

risks.label: Inventory Normalization
risks.evidence: Customers continue to focus on reducing their inventory levels.

risks.label: Gaming Segment Decline
risks.evidence: Revenue declined 17% year-over-year and 9% sequentially due to a decrease in semi-custom revenue.
